messages.author: 256c65e083a80aea
messages.subject: confusing scanone output
parts:
I am using scanone to map qtls on a data set derived from ngs. I have  35K variants as markers and am wish to identify QTLs for a single trait using 96 segregants of a haploid micro-organism in a simple cross between two strains. The genotypes have been assigned as AA or AB as for a BC. Prior to running scanone I just ran calc.genoprob as advised in the short tour tutorial.  Now the problem is that I have many loci that are giving LOD scores in excess of 3 with no obvious peaks. In the first round I noticed that I had one extreme outlier in the data set but the problem persisted even after removing that. I assume that the source of the problem is the large number of markers and that the high LOD scores are arising by chance.  How does one deal with this sort of problem and get a scan plot out that is informative as to whether there are any QTL detectable.

Thank you.

William

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] confusing scanone output
parts:
Rather than focusing on 3 as a threshold, I would use a permutation test to derive an appropriate significance threshold, and look at regions with LOD scores exceeding a permutation-based threshold.

karl
